title: Does a signal-reading door fleet help people once robots are not counted, and for whom?
summary: society-cheapcue found the crowd average, robots included, is worse under a reading fleet than under yield-all in all 35 cells, because robots that go against non-signallers collide. Here robots are dropped from the score and a planner weights urgent people's cost by λ (1 = plain average). With 30% robots, 20% urgent people, normal cue cost 0.6, collision cost 3 and dithering cost 1, the fleet helps people at λ = 1 only if the urgent cue costs them ≤ about 0.35 of what it costs normal people (gain +0.005 at ρ = 0.35, +0.017 at 0.25, +0.047 at 0); at ρ = 1 it hurts people at every λ tried (−0.078 at λ = 1, −0.124 at 5). At ρ = 0.25 a planner needs λ ≥ 0.71 to prefer it. A 10% misreading rate cuts the usable ρ at λ = 1 to 0.175 and 20% to 0; with 70% robots people lose even at ρ = 0.25 (−0.109). Mean field from society-fakeurgency, which was checked by simulation. Assumed, not sourced: ρ, cue costs and λ (swept), round-figure door costs, logit sharpness, no robot learning, random pairing.
lede: does a signal-reading door fleet help people once robots are not counted? Only if the urgent cue costs them about a third of what it costs others, or a planner weights urgent waiting; an equal-cost cue hurts people at every weight tried.
